BiblicalUsage: Kaphaph is to curve — to bow down, to bend the head or the knee. Isaiah asks whether a fast is to bow down the head as a bulrush; Micah asks whether he shall come before the LORD and bow himself before the high God; and the psalm says the LORD raiseth them that are bowed down.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the bowed head is the posture of the fast and of the prayer, and the God who sees the bowed head is the God who raises it again. He lifts the head that bows to Him.
